title: Kruger and Dunning's 1999 paper, and the later argument about statistics
summary: The original paper reports overconfidence among low performers. Later work has asked how much of the pattern is a statistical artifact.
body: Justin Kruger and David Dunning, "Unskilled and unaware of it: How difficulties in recognizing one's own incompetence lead to inflated self-assessments" (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1999), reported that people who scored low on certain tests overestimated their performance the most. The v1 article states that pattern as a fact about metacognition. Later papers have argued that part of the pattern can appear from regression and from noisy self-estimates even without a special metacognitive deficit. A specific critique was not opened, so that side is named and not quoted. The original claim stays tied to the 1999 paper. The interpretation is not settled.

contested_views.label: Kruger and Dunning 1999
contested_views.summary: Low performers overestimated themselves most, which the authors tied to a metacognitive deficit.

contested_views.label: Statistical-artifact critiques
contested_views.summary: Later methodological papers argue the graph can arise without that deficit. Those papers were not opened in this pass and need their own citations before they are quoted.
